title: Agents-as-Peers: Bias-Controlled LLM Evaluation as Multi-Agent Peer Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2602.02589v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluation commonly relies on fixed human-authored benchmarks or centralized human/model judges. Fixed benchmarks can age and enter model training corpora, while centralized judges introduce their own scoring preferences.   We cast LLM evaluation as a multi-agent peer-assessment problem and introduce Agents-as-Peers, a distributed evaluation protocol in which every agent generates tasks, answers the shared task set, and judges the answers of its peers, with no privileged evaluator.   Self-ratings are excluded from the ranking, and judging is repeated under controlled identity and presentation regimes so that self bias, identity effects, presentation-position sensitivity, and judge severity are measured rather than left implicit. translated_title: 智能体即同伴：将偏差受控的大语言模型评估形式化为多智能体同伴互评
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）评估通常依赖于固定的人类编写基准或集中式的人类/模型评判者。固定基准可能会过时并进入模型训练语料库，而集中式评判者则会引入自身的评分偏好。我们将大语言模型评估视为一个多智能体同伴互评问题，并提出了Agents-as-Peers——一种分布式评估协议，其中每个智能体负责生成任务、回答共享的任务集，并评判其同伴的答案，不存在任何特权评估者。自我评分被排除在排名之外，并且评判过程在受控的身份与呈现模式下重复进行，从而使自我偏差、身份效应、呈现位置敏感性和评判者严格性得到实际测量，而非保持隐含。在一个由12个大语言模型和420个智能体生成问题组成的实例化实验中，Agents-as-Peers在每个模式下聚合了55,440个非自我同伴评判。大多数智能体给自己的答案打分偏……（原文在此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出Agents-as-Peers分布式评估协议，让每个大语言模型智能体生成任务、回答共享任务集并互评同伴答案（排除自评），以解决固定基准老化和集中式评判者偏差问题，并对自我偏差、身份效应等评判偏差进行受控测量。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Agents-as-Peers, a distributed evaluation protocol in which every LLM agent generates tasks, answers a shared task set, and peer-judges others' answers without self-ratings, addressing benchmark aging and centralized judge bias while measurably controlling for self-bias, identity effects, and judge severity.
